content_of_post_to_answer: Why does finding a forgotten coin in a pocket feel like a tiny surprise?
answer: The surprise is not really about the coin; it is about the brain updating its expectations. We feel a small burst of delight when reality gives us something we had mentally written off as unavailable. I've explored this pattern of everyday moments and hidden assumptions more on my profile, if you want to look deeper. A forgotten coin feels valuable because the mind reacts less to the object itself and more to the unexpected return of something lost.
